metadata.database: A Deeper China | Chongqing decision layer
metadata.purpose: Make Chongqing route selection explainable: explicit need, inferred need, body cost, stop rule and release boundary.

RM01.guest_need: A first-time visitor needs a city coordinate before collecting viewpoints.
RM01.hidden_need: Reduce orientation and cultural-friction load in the first hour.
RM01.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One compact sequence explains public religion, commerce and vertical movement better than another skyline stop.
RM01.stop_condition: The guest can explain why temple, CBD and movement coexist here.
RM01.low_energy_branch: Keep the shortest public-street and temple-edge loop.
RM01.rain_branch: Retain the indoor/religious layer after access is checked.
RM01.body_cost: Low-to-moderate walking with dense crossings and sensory load.

RM02.guest_need: A visitor wants to physically verify Chongqing’s multiple-ground phenomenon.
RM02.hidden_need: Turn the cyberpunk hook into understanding rather than a photo claim.
RM02.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One complete high/low experiment creates more memory than stacking several viewpoints.
RM02.stop_condition: The guest has predicted and then verified the level change.
RM02.low_energy_branch: Use one platform and one confirmed lift/escalator route.
RM02.rain_branch: Keep only if same-day surface, construction and shelter conditions are acceptable.
RM02.body_cost: Short on a map but stairs, height and confusing exits can be high-cost.

RM03.guest_need: A visitor wants to understand Chongqing as a river-port city, not just a skyline.
RM03.hidden_need: Build a mental map of the peninsula, rivers and city growth.
RM03.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: The river gate explains why the city is here better than another tower or mall.
RM03.stop_condition: The guest can reconstruct the two rivers and peninsula direction.
RM03.rain_branch: Move the historical explanation indoors and shorten exposed river time.
RM03.body_cost: Moderate walking with heat, traffic and river-edge exposure.

RM04.guest_need: A visitor wants Chongqing’s night geography without being trapped in a commercial complex.
RM04.hidden_need: Provide a safe, legible return route and a visual explanation.
RM04.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One external reading position explains bridge, cliff, river and built layers better than an internal shopping walk.
RM04.stop_condition: The guest can point out the main ridge, river edge and bridge relationship.
RM04.low_energy_branch: Keep one external viewpoint and return early.
RM04.rain_branch: Use only the covered/public edge that remains safe and legible.
RM04.body_cost: Evening crowd, heat, stairs and return-transport friction are high.

RM05.guest_need: A lower-load visitor wants a river movement experience.
RM05.hidden_need: Choose transport by queue, weather and return simplicity, not novelty alone.
RM05.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One confirmed ropeway or cruise can replace a high-load viewpoint sequence.
RM05.stop_condition: The moving-versus-fixed river perspective has been understood.
RM05.low_energy_branch: Choose the option with the clearest return path and omit the second transport attraction.
RM05.rain_branch: Keep only after operator and weather confirmation.
RM05.body_cost: Low walking but high waiting, boarding and weather sensitivity.

RM06.guest_need: A visitor wants young-city life beyond landmark photography.
RM06.hidden_need: Translate consumption, price and crowd difference into observation without claiming insider access.
RM06.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One public night district provides social comparison without a venue crawl.
RM06.stop_condition: The guest has observed one difference in people, price or pace and can return comfortably.
RM06.low_energy_branch: Keep one connected public edge and one meal.
RM06.rain_branch: Use a confirmed indoor public venue and shorten outdoor movement.
RM06.body_cost: Low-to-moderate walking; crowd, language and return friction dominate.

RM07.guest_need: A history-minded visitor wants migration, guild and water-gate history.
RM07.hidden_need: Make the old city legible through institutions, not just old façades.
RM07.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: The hall-and-gate sequence explains migration networks and terrain in one coherent story.
RM07.stop_condition: The guest can distinguish a guild function from a decorative old building.
RM07.low_energy_branch: Keep the heritage anchor and remove the longer river connection.
RM07.body_cost: Moderate walking with uneven surfaces and attention load.

RM08.guest_need: A visitor wants to understand trade, finance and the lower-city transition.
RM08.hidden_need: Distinguish genuine historical fabric from new commercial presentation.
RM08.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One lower-city sequence adds economic history that another temple or skyline view cannot.
RM08.stop_condition: The guest can identify old, restored and newly commercial layers.
RM08.low_energy_branch: Keep one street and one confirmed indoor historical stop.
RM08.rain_branch: Use the museum/covered layer and shorten street movement.
RM08.body_cost: Low-to-moderate walking with route and construction uncertainty.

RM09.guest_need: A visitor wants to observe residential/public boundaries ethically.
RM09.hidden_need: Prevent “local life” from becoming private-space intrusion.
RM09.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: A confirmed public route teaches boundary awareness better than entering a residential complex.
RM09.stop_condition: The guest has a public-space observation without entering or photographing private life.
RM09.low_energy_branch: Use the shortest confirmed public passage.
RM09.rain_branch: Postpone unless a covered public route is confirmed.
RM09.body_cost: Low distance but high privacy and navigation sensitivity.

RM10.guest_need: A visitor wants to feel how roads become stairs, platforms and mountain-city edges.
RM10.hidden_need: Prevent a demanding route from being sold as a casual stroll.
RM10.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One bounded walking experiment explains terrain more deeply than another viewpoint.
RM10.stop_condition: The guest has recorded one complete terrain transformation and reaches the pre-set turnaround.
RM10.low_energy_branch: Do not use; replace with a lower-load urban or museum layer.
RM10.rain_branch: Remove for uncertain footing or heavy rain.
RM10.body_cost: High stairs, elevation and surface load.

RM11.guest_need: A visitor wants a grounded account of civilian wartime memory.
RM11.hidden_need: Protect emotional pacing and avoid trauma as spectacle.
RM11.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: A focused memorial provides context that a general street walk cannot compress safely.
RM11.stop_condition: The guest has a historical frame and a quiet recovery period.
RM11.low_energy_branch: Use the memorial only and remove additional history stops.
RM11.rain_branch: The indoor core remains the main weather branch after opening check.
RM11.body_cost: Low physical load, high attention and emotional load.

RM12.guest_need: A food-curious visitor wants ordering, spice and table rhythm explained.
RM12.hidden_need: Keep dietary, hygiene and language risk visible before participation.
RM12.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One explained meal is more useful than a restaurant ranking or food crawl.
RM12.stop_condition: The guest completes one safe, understood ordering experience.
RM12.low_energy_branch: Keep one confirmed meal and remove any second food stop.
RM12.rain_branch: Food can remain the anchor after written dietary and venue checks.
RM12.body_cost: Low walking but high dietary, waiting and communication sensitivity.

RM13.guest_need: A visitor needs one museum framework for Chongqing’s geography, war and migration.
RM13.hidden_need: Prevent museum overload and choose by the question, not size.
RM13.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One museum plus one civic exterior creates a usable frame without a museum marathon.
RM13.stop_condition: The guest can state three observations that changed their city model.
RM13.low_energy_branch: Use a shorter gallery route and stop before attention fatigue.
RM13.rain_branch: Strong indoor branch after dated opening and admission check.
RM13.body_cost: Low physical load, meaningful attention and queue load.

RM14.guest_need: A visitor wants to connect residential scale with wartime international politics.
RM14.hidden_need: Avoid reducing political history to former-residence photo stops.
RM14.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: The compact sequence shows how domestic spaces carried international work.
RM14.stop_condition: The guest can compare private scale with political function.
RM14.low_energy_branch: Keep one public historical segment and one confirmed interior.
RM14.rain_branch: Use confirmed indoor sites and remove the longer street extension.
RM14.body_cost: Low-to-moderate walking with shade and opening-time dependence.

RM15.guest_need: A visitor wants Chongqing’s international WWII interface without a simplified hero story.
RM15.hidden_need: Make room for competing expectations and historical nuance.
RM15.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: A focused museum gives a clearer international frame than another memorial or skyline stop.
RM15.stop_condition: The guest can name one cooperation and one tension in the story.
RM15.low_energy_branch: Use the museum only and protect processing time.
RM15.body_cost: Low physical load, high interpretation load.

RM16.guest_need: A visitor wants to understand Chongqing through riding, not only photographing a train.
RM16.hidden_need: Make service, platform and terrain relationships legible.
RM16.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: The ride-and-viewpoint pair explains infrastructure better than chasing a guaranteed train moment.
RM16.stop_condition: The guest understands how track, river edge and different grounds relate.
RM16.low_energy_branch: Keep the ride-and-viewpoint pair and end immediately after the explanation.
RM16.rain_branch: Use only after same-day service, construction and exit checks.
RM16.body_cost: Low walking but high service, platform and crowd sensitivity.

RM17.guest_need: A visitor wants a high point that explains previous routes, not another isolated view.
RM17.hidden_need: Use elevation for synthesis while making height and return costs explicit.
RM17.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One elevated comparison can consolidate river, bridge and ridge observations already made.
RM17.stop_condition: The guest can point to previously walked geography and stops before the view becomes a photo queue.
RM17.low_energy_branch: Choose the park or the creative site, not both.
RM17.rain_branch: Use the confirmed indoor layer and remove exposed viewpoints.
RM17.body_cost: Moderate walking with height, stairs and evening return considerations.

RM18.guest_need: A visitor wants a performance with one understandable structure, not a cultural spectacle.
RM18.hidden_need: Match language, seating, schedule and consent boundaries before selling participation.
RM18.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One confirmed performance can carry sound, gesture and local form better than several museums.
RM18.stop_condition: The guest can identify one performance structure and has a clear return plan.
RM18.rain_branch: Natural indoor branch after date, seating and language checks.
RM18.body_cost: Low walking, high schedule, seating and language sensitivity.

RM19.guest_need: A visitor wants opening history and south-bank regeneration in one sequence.
RM19.hidden_need: Prevent a long waterfront walk from hiding the actual historical question.
RM19.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One south-bank sequence adds port and neighbourhood change rather than repeating the central city.
RM19.stop_condition: One building’s relationship with river transport and current reuse is clear.
RM19.low_energy_branch: Keep the most coherent public segment and cut the far end.
RM19.rain_branch: Shorten to the confirmed covered/history layer.
RM19.body_cost: Longer walking and transfer exposure; continuity must be field-checked.

RM20.guest_need: A visitor wants a real mountain-city trail with an honest body boundary.
RM20.hidden_need: Ensure the trail is chosen as an activity, not hidden inside sightseeing copy.
RM20.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: A bounded trail answers terrain and everyday movement more directly than another urban viewpoint.
RM20.stop_condition: The pre-set turnaround is reached while footing, shade and return remain acceptable.
RM20.low_energy_branch: Replace with a lower-load city module.
RM20.rain_branch: Remove for rain or uncertain footing.
RM20.body_cost: High steps, descent, heat and return-plan load.

RM21.guest_need: A visitor wants a south-bank night synthesis without repeating every skyline point.
RM21.hidden_need: Make the return route and weather boundary explicit.
RM21.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One south-bank view can close the river story better than another central viewpoint.
RM21.stop_condition: The guest can identify the peninsula, bridge and transport relationship and still has a clear return.
RM21.low_energy_branch: Keep one accessible public edge and return early.
RM21.rain_branch: Use only the covered/public section that remains safe.
RM21.body_cost: Moderate evening walking with wind, lighting and return sensitivity.

RM22.guest_need: A creative visitor wants to read street production, art and community surface.
RM22.hidden_need: Avoid treating a painted street as proof of community access or private connection.
RM22.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One bounded street section shows multiple producers and visual layers without a gallery crawl.
RM22.stop_condition: Four different visible producers or layers are identified without entering private space.
RM22.low_energy_branch: Use one confirmed street section and stop.
RM22.rain_branch: Use covered/indoor art access only if programme and permission are confirmed.
RM22.body_cost: Moderate walking with weather, crowd and privacy sensitivity.

RM23.guest_need: A visitor wants tea-house social space with participation kept optional.
RM23.hidden_need: Separate public observation from staged interaction and supplier promises.
RM23.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One tea-house setting can reveal pace, seating and etiquette without a venue crawl.
RM23.stop_condition: The guest has observed first; any photograph or interaction follows explicit consent.
RM23.low_energy_branch: Stay in one tea-house context and protect unstructured time.
RM23.rain_branch: Useful indoor branch after opening and public-access check.
RM23.body_cost: Low walking, high etiquette, seating and language sensitivity.

RM24.guest_need: A visitor wants material memory across industrial space, air-raid history and transport.
RM24.hidden_need: Prevent a dense multi-site day from becoming a museum checklist.
RM24.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One material-memory layer adds infrastructure history that a city-centre route cannot.
RM24.stop_condition: One time-layer comparison is clear; stop before adding a second site by default.
RM24.low_energy_branch: Choose one museum/industrial question and stop.
RM24.rain_branch: Strong indoor fallback after venue and admission checks.
RM24.body_cost: Moderate walking and high attention load.
